P1.evidence: Best open in the batch. Setter notes were read back three separate times and used to make the prospect feel known — 'Kim gave me some context. So, you've been working out like weighted calisthenics for a while, yeah?', 'from Kim, he told me, like, you've been, like, what's been missing is a little bit of structure. Is that correct?', and 'I remember Kim asked you, like, you're from Bahia, right?' The frame was set as a two-part sequencing promise rather than the four-part version — 'Before we dive in, just want to make sure I actually understand your situation. So, before we get into any details about the program' — and agreement was requested and given ('Cool?'). No standalone open question; the rep went straight into the setter's material, which worked here but skips the check.

P2.evidence: Injuries were asked directly and early, the only call in the batch where that happened before any recommendation: 'Sorry to interject, did you had any injuries doing that?' Training week asked ('So how many days do you work out per week, every day?'), work asked ('you as a doctor, you probably work long hours, or not?'), diet asked and probed at length including fasting protocol and cheat meals. Body composition was pursued properly — 'Have you measured your fat tissue?' — though age, height and weight were all volunteered rather than asked. The gap that matters: no health-conditions question at all. The prospect happens to be a physician with nothing to disclose, so nothing was missed here, but the check did not run. Sleep was raised only prospectively about the coming baby, never as current quantity and quality.

P3.evidence: Strongest goals work in the batch. The prioritisation question ran cleanly — 'which one of these would be the most important thing for you? Like in six months, like if you had to choose' — and was followed with the why: 'Why conditioning is so important?', which produced the real answer about being a busy doctor with a second child coming. Specific targets were pursued rather than accepted vaguely: 'do you have, like, a specific goal in terms of muscle? How much muscle you would like to gain?' and the body-fat number. The future-state question ran: 'if we get it dialed in... what would be different? How would you operate if you would have the dial-in?' The impact-on-others and legacy layers were supplied by the rep instead of elicited — 'your purpose is be more healthy, be more mobile, to play around with your two daughters' — and the summary at 00:26:02 restated the mechanics accurately but never made the 'this isn't really about X' move.

P4.evidence: The single best root-cause question in the batch, and it was framed to respect the prospect's expertise: 'you clearly have, like, you know your stuff, yeah? So you've researched training extensively, and you've been doing this for years. So what's held you back from getting that conditioning and mobility piece dialed in on your own?' The prospect named the gap himself and precisely — 'mainly for me is structure, is combining with what to do, in what day, for how long, and what to do' — which is exactly what P4e asks for. The rep then extended it into overtraining risk. What did not run: any history of specific programmes tried and abandoned, and the information-isn't-the-problem line was embedded in the question rather than stated.

P5.evidence: Never run. No two-year question, no settle test, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep did raise a future risk — 'when your second child will appear in this world, you're probably going to have less time and less sleep' — but used it to sell accountability rather than to build a cost of inaction, and the prospect corrected the framing ('I don't believe it's actually busy... it's tiredness and lack of sleep'). With no consequence built, the timing objection at 00:48:40 had nothing to push against, and the rep answered it by reshaping the product instead.

P6.evidence: The all-in question ran essentially verbatim and in the right place, before any number: 'if you had all those three things, like the structure, kettlebell programming built around your calisthenics, the nutrition dialed in, and someone who is in your corner supporting you all the way, would there be any reason you wouldn't commit to this?' The answer — 'Mainly cost' — was isolated immediately ('Apart from that') and cleared. The rep then confirmed commitment before pricing: 'if you can figure out the details, the investment side, you're fully committed to showing up and doing the work.' The belief check that the structure would get him there was implied rather than asked outright, so P6a is partial. Worth noting the rep also ran a commitment-timing question much earlier, at 00:24:09: 'is this something that you're really actually wanting to commit right now? Or like three months from now, six months from now?'

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — price stated, 'how would you like to proceed', payment methods explained, and a direct ask for a deposit figure — but no payment was collected and the prospect declined to name any amount. Onboarding, the agreement and the welcome sequence were therefore unreachable.

objection_plays.detail: Cost was named as the only blocker. The isolate ran properly — 'just make sure apart from the finances right now, is there anything standing in a way from moving forward?' — and got a clean answer. Break-it-up ran thoroughly and, to the rep's credit, honestly: two, three and six payment options with the higher total disclosed out loud. Not run: the should-I-versus-how frame, the permission question for an open financial conversation, and five of the six financial-picture questions. The one attempt at cash on hand came very late and in an unusual form — 'how much would you be actually willing to put down today? Just to see how it looks like' — and the prospect declined to answer, at which point the play stopped.

'August, September, and October will be difficult months for me because my wife will be very pregnant.' Two moves landed: the change-question, 'what's going to change between now and sometime in the future?', and a light cost-of-priority jab, 'Come on, barbecue or your health?' The scripted core did not run — no 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep also mis-stated the interval, calling an October birth 'six months from now' on a call dated 28 May, which weakened rather than strengthened the point.

'I still have to think about it, man.' The rep asked for a timeframe and pressed on what would change, which are the useful parts, and got a substantive answer about the practice restructure. None of the decision-framing moves ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the man you want to be, how does he decide right now'. Given the prospect had already validated both the plan and the price, this was the play with the most left on the table.

'I have to take a little moment to think about that and involve the wife because we have a lot of projects now for this year' at 00:45:06. Not one OB move ran, and the rep never returned to it — despite having established earlier that the wife trains, does CrossFit, gets frustrated when she cannot train, and is herself a doctor, which is about as favourable a setup for 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger' as the script could ask for.

Script gap — currency. USD pricing converts to roughly R$25,000-28,000 for the six-month tier and about R$20,000 for the three-month one, and the prospect did the arithmetic himself as the reason he could not proceed. This is the second call in this batch where a non-US prospect priced the offer in home currency and stalled on it, after the New Zealand call on 05/25. Nothing in the playbook addresses local pricing, FX or regional terms, so the rep had no move and cut the term instead.

Script gap — product-combination proof. The prospect's central question all call was whether kettlebell programming can be integrated without losing his weighted calisthenics strength, and he raised it a third time as his one remaining doubt at 00:42:49. There is no scripted way to demonstrate programme design pre-sale, so the rep deferred to the coach: 'this is tailored to your needs, so whatever you will discuss with Trevor he will build a program around that.' A sample week would have answered it.

notes: The best-run call in the batch on discovery — setter notes read back, injuries screened before recommending anything, goals driven to specifics, and a root-cause question that respected a subject-matter expert without conceding the sale. Two things cost it. The consequence frame never ran, so a genuinely warm prospect who had already validated the price had nothing pulling him to act now rather than in a month. And the wife objection was voiced clearly and never touched, on a call where the spouse is an athlete and a doctor and was the easiest ally available.
